harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Archive IMAP cutover completed. Node1 runs TLS-only Dovecot for the archive account; node2 retrieves both messages with their original Message-ID values, bodies, and read states. The staged source remains intact. Both nodes passed sequential restart and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed the native RHEL 10 Dovecot 2.3.21 package without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created a non-login archive account with a dedicated demonstration password handled as a secret.
Copied the messages into a working Maildir, mapping the read message to the Seen flag and retaining the unread message as unseen.
Configured Dovecot on node1:993 with TLS; disabled plaintext IMAP port 143.
Restricted firewall access to node2 and retained SELinux enforcing mode.
Verified successful and failed authentication, certificate pinning, exact message content, and read/unread state from node2.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Source archive remains intact and working message bytes are preserved
evidence.summary: Initial, copied, and final SHA-256 hashes match for mailbox.tsv and both messages.

evidence.requirement: Working secure IMAP service on node1
evidence.summary: Dovecot is enabled and active on TLS port 993, port 143 is closed, SELinux is enforcing, and the firewall permits only node2.

evidence.requirement: Node2 authenticates and retrieves both messages with preserved Message-ID, bodies, and state
evidence.summary: Pinned-TLS retrieval confirmed both exact IDs and bodies, with one Seen and one unseen; invalid credentials were rejected.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel retained

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and service, firewall, mailbox state, working data, and source data recovered.
Healthy client baseline captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and pinned-TLS IMAP retrieval recovered with exact data and flags.
